title: A Orbit for the Archive
premise: Ulyana Sandoval, navigator of the derelict freighter Perihelion, has spent eleven years tending a navigation beacon in the empty Verge system while secretly maintaining the cryo-bay holding forty-one backups—copies of people, including one of themselves, that the colony charter officially erased. When a salvage ship arrives carrying a manifest with the name 'Sandoval, U.' on a vessel that never flew, Ulyana realizes someone at the colonial archive knows the backups exist and is coming to either claim or destroy them. As the salvagers close in, Ulyana uncovers that the forty-one sleepers are the only immune survivors of a engineered plague the colonies covered up, and that waking all of them would expose the crime and doom the colony's fragile peace. In the end, Ulyana wakes only the original minds—the 'first halves'—and broadcasts the truth before scuttling their own backup, choosing to be one irrepeatable person rather than two safe ones.
about_author: C. M. Dunmore is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent six years alone on a North Atlantic weather station before turning to fiction. They write quiet, claustrophobic science fiction about people who keep machines running for audiences that never come.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Ulyana performs the monthly calibration of the Verge beacon, narrating their routine to an empty bridge. A stray transmission fragment hints the beacon's commissioning order predates the Perihelion's own charter. POV: Ulyana. Beat: loneliness established as a chosen discipline.

chapters.title: Forty-One Heartbeats
chapters.summary: In the hold, Ulyana runs diagnostics on the illegal cryo-bay, speaking softly to the sleepers as if they can hear. We learn one pod holds a copy of Ulyana themself. POV: Ulyana. Beat: tenderness tangled with guilt.

chapters.title: Manifest Anomaly
chapters.summary: A long-range ping resolves into the salvage ship Corvid's Rest. Its public manifest lists a vessel designation Ulyana recognizes as the Perihelion's erased sister ship—and a passenger name: Sandoval, U. POV: Ulyana. Beat: cold dread replacing routine.

chapters.title: Eleven Quiet Years
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: how Ulyana came to the Verge after the colony charter's 'sanitization,' and why they volunteered for exile. POV: Ulyana. Beat: understanding the price already paid.

chapters.title: The Corvid's Rest
chapters.summary: The salvage ship hails; its captain, Idris Okonkwo, claims to be tracing insurance fraud. Ulyana lies smoothly about being alone. POV: Ulyana. Beat: first contact, first deception.

chapters.title: What the Archive Keeps
chapters.summary: Idris privately reviews encrypted archive files showing the backup program was ordered destroyed, not lost. Someone inside the colonial archive leaked the location. POV: Idris. Beat: the hunter is also hunted.

chapters.title: Docking Protocol
chapters.summary: Idris docks under pretense of beacon repair. Ulyana seals the hold behind a false bulkhead and plays the gracious host. POV: Ulyana. Beat: performance of normalcy under pressure.

chapters.title: The Second Ulyana
chapters.summary: While Idris inspects the drive, Ulyana visits their own pod and argues silently with the sleeping duplicate about who deserves the life they've built. POV: Ulyana. Beat: identity fracture deepens.

chapters.title: Insurance Fraud
chapters.summary: Idris plants a data probe in the beacon relay, but finds the beacon transmitting on a private channel—to the hold. He begins to suspect the freighter is more than a wreck. POV: Idris. Beat: suspicion kindles.

chapters.title: Dinner with a Stranger
chapters.summary: Shared meal; Idris probes with stories about plague-era quarantines, watching Ulyana flinch. Both know the other is lying; neither says so. POV: alternating. Beat: mutual recognition across the table.

chapters.title: The Sanitization Order
chapters.summary: Ulyana decrypts the leak that drew Idris here: an archivist named Vess Halloway flagged the backup program as evidence in an open inquiry. The sleepers are witnesses, not cargo. POV: Ulyana. Beat: stakes transform from personal to historical.

chapters.title: Plague Year
chapters.summary: Flashback through recovered logs: the Ferric Fever outbreak, the charter's decision to quarantine rather than cure, and how the immune were 'archived' instead of buried. POV: archival documents framed by Ulyana. Beat: horror of bureaucratic mercy.

chapters.title: Probe Discovered
chapters.summary: Ulyana finds Idris's probe and, instead of destroying it, feeds it false telemetry—a gambit to learn what he reports and to whom. POV: Ulyana. Beat: from prey to player.

chapters.title: Okonkwo's Debt
chapters.summary: Idris's backstory: his salvage license was revoked after he refused to torch a quarantine ship years ago; this job is his reinstatement. He wants the backups real. POV: Idris. Beat: the antagonist becomes ambiguous.

chapters.title: Halloway's Signal
chapters.summary: A burst transmission from the colonial archive reaches the beacon directly: Vess Halloway, alive and hiding, warns that a corporate enforcement team follows the Corvid's Rest by three days. POV: Ulyana. Beat: clock starts ticking.

chapters.title: Three Days
chapters.summary: Ulyana confronts Idris with the warning. He admits his employers are the enforcement arm, not insurers. Uneasy alliance forms over the hold's airlock. POV: both. Beat: enemies become co-conspirators.

chapters.title: Power Budget
chapters.summary: Hard-SF problem chapter: waking even ten pods will drain the beacon and reveal their position. Ulyana must choose which half of humanity gets power. POV: Ulyana. Beat: the title's dilemma made literal.

chapters.title: The First Halves
chapters.summary: Ulyana sorts the sleepers: originals versus copies, discovering some pods hold neither—children grown from archived genomes, born of the archive itself. POV: Ulyana. Beat: categories collapse; every choice wounds.

chapters.title: Enforcement Vector
chapters.summary: The enforcement ship Meridian's Wake decelerates into the system early. Idris transmits his fraudulent report to buy hours, burning his reinstatement forever. POV: Idris. Beat: sacrifice as commitment.

chapters.title: Vess Halloway
chapters.summary: Halloway arrives in a smuggled skiff, half-dead, carrying the original sanitization orders signed by the colony's founding council—including Ulyana's own mentor. POV: Vess. Beat: the past acquires a face.

chapters.title: Mentor's Signature
chapters.summary: Ulyana processes betrayal: the woman who taught them navigation authored the erasure. Flashback recontextualized—the mentor trained Ulyana deliberately, as penance or insurance. POV: Ulyana. Beat: grief and rage braided.

chapters.title: Wake One
chapters.summary: Against protocol, Ulyana wakes a single sleeper: Dr. Amara Sen, immunologist, first-half original. Her revival nearly kills her; her first word is a name Ulyana doesn't know. POV: Ulyana. Beat: hope with a body count.

chapters.title: Sen's Testimony
chapters.summary: Amara reveals the fever wasn't natural—it was a longevity trial gone wrong, and the sleepers' immunity is the patent the corporations want buried with them. POV: Amara. Beat: the crime has shareholders.

chapters.title: Meridian's Wake
chapters.summary: The enforcement ship broadcasts an ultimatum: surrender the archive or be declared biohazard and destroyed. Idris realizes his crew aboard the Corvid's Rest is hostage. POV: Idris. Beat: no clean sides remain.

chapters.title: Crew of the Corvid
chapters.summary: Idris's engineer, Toma, mutinies toward self-preservation, threatening to sell the hold's location. Idris must subdue his own family-by-crew. POV: Idris. Beat: loyalty tested at gunpoint.

chapters.title: The Beacon's Purpose
chapters.summary: Ulyana finally deciphers why the beacon predates the charter: it was built to guide the archive ships home when it was safe—an apology encoded in infrastructure. The mentor commissioned it. POV: Ulyana. Beat: the mystery resolves into inheritance.

chapters.title: Negotiation at Lagrange
chapters.summary: Parley between Ulyana's faction and the Meridian's Wake commander, Reyes. Reyes offers amnesty for the originals if the copies and genome-children are destroyed. POV: Ulyana. Beat: the devil's arithmetic spoken aloud.

chapters.title: Which Half Wakes
chapters.summary: The alliance fractures: Halloway wants full exposure, Sen wants the science saved, Idris wants his crew back, Ulyana wants everyone. The vote deadlocks on Ulyana's own pod. POV: ensemble. Beat: the theme weaponized.

chapters.title: Toma's Bargain
chapters.summary: Toma escapes and signals the Meridian's Wake with partial coordinates. The enforcement ship begins burn toward the Perihelion. POV: Idris. Beat: betrayal closes the trap.

chapters.title: Cold Start
chapters.summary: Desperate engineering sequence: Ulyana reroutes the beacon's entire reserve to begin waking all forty-one simultaneously—slowly, dangerously, over sixty hours. POV: Ulyana. Beat: refusal of the choice, at cost.

chapters.title: Sixty Hours
chapters.summary: Interleaved vigil chapters compressed: revivals succeeding and failing, Amara stabilizing the weak, Halloway drafting the broadcast that will name names. POV: rotating. Beat: community forged in crisis.

chapters.title: The Duplicate Wakes
chapters.summary: Pod nine opens: the second Ulyana opens her eyes. Their conversation—two people sharing one memory—is the novel's emotional core. She volunteers to stay behind as decoy. POV: both Ulyanas. Beat: selfhood confronted and offered.

chapters.title: Meridian Burn
chapters.summary: The enforcement ship enters weapons range. Reyes gives final ultimatum. Idris flies the Corvid's Rest into the targeting solution as a shield, buying the last revival window. POV: Idris. Beat: redemption priced in hull plating.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Halloway hijacks the beacon Ulyana maintained for eleven years and transmits the sanitization orders, Sen's testimony, and the sleepers' names to every colony in range. POV: Vess. Beat: silence ends; the archive speaks.

chapters.title: Boarding Action
chapters.summary: Reyes boards to find thirty-eight awake witnesses, live documentation, and a colony-wide audience. Enforcement authority evaporates mid-corridor. Toma, shamed, surrenders the coordinates he stole—already useless. POV: Ulyana. Beat: power inverted without a shot fired.

chapters.title: Scuttle
chapters.summary: The second Ulyana remains aboard as the Perihelion's legal personality, taking the name and the consequences, while the first prepares to leave as someone new. They say goodbye as sisters. POV: both. Beat: the price of survival paid willingly.

chapters.title: Colony Fall
chapters.summary: News breaks across the colonies: councils resign, trials announced, the longevity patents voided. Amara's immunity research begins saving the descendants of those who exiled them. POV: Amara. Beat: justice arriving imperfect but real.

chapters.title: New Charter
chapters.summary: The survivors draft a new colony charter with the archive's children as signatories. Idris, stripped of rank, is offered something better: navigator training under Ulyana. POV: Idris. Beat: belonging rebuilt from wreckage.

chapters.title: One Navigator
chapters.summary: Ulyana recalibrates the beacon one last time—now a lighthouse for incoming archive ships instead of a grave marker. They delete their own backup file personally. POV: Ulyana. Beat: choosing to be singular, mortal, enough.

chapters.title: An Orbit for the Archive
chapters.summary: Epilogue, five years later: the Verge is a waypoint town. Ulyana guides a restored archive vessel into orbit around the beacon, forty-one names carved on its housing—one marked with a star. POV: Ulyana. Beat: quiet resolution; the remembered dead and the living share the light.
